label: Claude Fable 5.2
output:
Here's the post, at 427 words and roughly 2,350 characters with spaces.

@Kavya's post yesterday about founders DMing engineers in their own cohort with 40% hikes is about me. Most of our Foundry91 batch has figured that out and some of you have tagged me, so I will say my side once and take the rest offline.

First, what I got wrong. Two engineers from SitterNest joined us at DabbaDost on 3 November. I knew where they worked from day one. I should have called Kavya before any offer went out. I messaged her only after the second offer was accepted, and that is the wrong order. This part is on me. Kavya, I am sorry.

Now the parts that are not accurate. I am putting them down because the numbers keep getting repeated in the comments.

1. Nobody from DabbaDost DMed anyone. We put a backend developer opening on our LinkedIn page and on Instahyre on 14 September, open to all. The first engineer applied on his own on 19 September. The second came two weeks later as his referral.

2. The hike was 22% over current CTC, for both. Not 40%.

3. The ESOPs are real. Our pool is small, but it exists and has been on paper since January.

I am not naming the two engineers and I request everyone in the comments to do the same. They applied for a job, got it and joined. They did not ask to be part of a LinkedIn thread.

Some context for people who don't know the two of us. Before demo day in March our Razorpay webhooks were a complete mess, and Kavya sat with me in the Koramangala office till 1am fixing them. It was not her company or her problem. I have never forgotten that. She is a good friend, she has helped me a lot, and she has every right to be upset about how she found out.

This will also happen again, to all of us. We are 11 startups hiring from the same small pool in HSR and Koramangala, and people will keep applying across companies. So I want to suggest one simple rule for cohort 4:

If you are interviewing someone from another batch company, you give that founder a heads up before the offer goes out.

Nobody needs permission to hire or to change jobs. But no founder should hear it after the fact on WhatsApp, the way Kavya did. I broke this rule before it existed and I will follow it from now on.

Kavya, coffee or a call, any day this week, whenever you are okay with it.

Two things before you post:

- **Tag:** I only had her first name, so retype the @Kavya at the top in LinkedIn and pick her from the dropdown, otherwise it won't link.
- **Blue tick:** I left out that she didn't reply to your WhatsApp. In public it would read as a dig at her, and the post is stronger with the timing mistake being only yours.
